The outlined treatment plan for acute bacterial sinusitis is appropriate. The use of amoxicillin-clavulanate is a first-line antibiotic recommendation for acute bacterial sinusitis in many clinical guidelines, particularly when symptoms are severe or persistent. Nasal saline irrigation helps clear mucus and reduce inflammation, while oral decongestants provide symptomatic relief. Advising the patient to return if symptoms persist beyond seven days or worsen is standard practice to monitor for complications or treatment failure.
